records.title: Introduction to African American Studies
records.header: AFRAM 101 Introduction to African American Studies (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 101 Introduction to African American Studies (5) SSc, DIV History, culture, religion, institutions, politics, economics, arts, and psychology of peoples of African descent as developed from experience in both the old and new worlds. Multidisciplinary analysis of social life from a black perspective as illustrated in selected historical and contemporary writings.

records.title: Introduction to African American History
records.header: AFRAM 150 Introduction to African American History (5) SSc
records.text: AFRAM 150 Introduction to African American History (5) SSc Introductory survey of topics and problems in African American history with some attention to Africa as well as to America. Basic introductory course for sequence of lecture courses and seminars in African American history. Offered: jointly with HSTAA 150.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Introduction African American Literature
records.header: AFRAM 214 Introduction African American Literature (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 214 Introduction African American Literature (5) A&H, DIV Introduction to various genres of African American literature from its beginnings to the present. Emphasizes the cultural and historical context of African American literary expression and its aesthetics criteria. Explores key issues and debates, such as race and racism, inequality, literary form, and canonical acceptance. Offered: jointly with ENGL 258.

records.title: African American Film Studies
records.header: AFRAM 220 African American Film Studies (5) A&H/SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 220 African American Film Studies (5) A&H/SSc, DIV Examines the history and theory of African American filmmaking, introducing central political and aesthetic debates by way of different cinematic eras, genres, and filmmakers. Focuses primarily on black directors and producers independent and commercial contexts as they confront popular representations of U.S. blackness in their own cinematic practice.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: The United States During the Era of Civil War and Reconstruction
records.header: AFRAM 241 The United States During the Era of Civil War and Reconstruction (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 241 The United States During the Era of Civil War and Reconstruction (5) SSc, DIV Views American Civil War and Reconstruction through lens of African-American social history. From U.S. government's abolition of Atlantic slave trade in 1808 to expanding Jim Crow laws in 1890s, reports how changes in the era were racialized and gendered. Considers how ideas of race, gender, class, and freedom in the U.S. were challenged and reshaped. Explores historical legacies of Civil War and Reconstruction from the nineteenth-century to now. Offered: jointly with HSTAA 241.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: African American Politics
records.header: AFRAM 246 African American Politics (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 246 African American Politics (5) SSc, DIV Survey of African Americans within the U.S. socio-political processes. Situates African Americans within a post-civil rights context where there is debate about race's centrality to an African American politics. Offered: jointly with POL S 246.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: African American Family
records.header: AFRAM 260 African American Family (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 260 African American Family (5) SSc, DIV Explores cultural processes as well as political, economic, and social structures and policies that have shaped, and continue to shape, the ways in which African American families have formed and functioned. Examines the history, experiences, struggles, and progress of African American families in the U.S. beginning with pre-Colonial Africa and ending with current issues facing African American families. Offered: jointly with SOC 260.

records.title: The African American Experience through Literature
records.header: AFRAM 261 The African American Experience through Literature (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: AFRAM 261 The African American Experience through Literature (5) A&H/SSc Instructs students in hermeneutical and sociological methods of analyses. Analyzes selected novels, essays, poems, short stories, and plays with the purpose of understanding the structures and functions of both society and personality. Offered: jointly with SOC 261.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: The Jazz Age
records.header: AFRAM 270 The Jazz Age (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 270 The Jazz Age (5) SSc, DIV Interdisciplinary study of period after World War I to Great Crash. African American and Anglo American currents and impulses that flowed together in the Roaring Twenties. Covers politics of normalcy, economics of margin, literature of indulgence and confusion, transformation of race relations, and cultural influence of jazz. Offered: jointly with HSTAA 270.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: History of the South Since the Civil War
records.header: AFRAM 272 History of the South Since the Civil War (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 272 History of the South Since the Civil War (5) SSc, DIV Reconstruction and its aftermath, the Agrarian (Populist) revolt, disfranchisement and segregation, the effects of urbanization and subsequent depression, desegregation, and the struggle for civil rights. Examines the New South, the conflict of ideology with structural and material change, and the place of the South in contemporary America.

records.title: Black Identities and Political Power
records.header: AFRAM 315 Black Identities and Political Power (5) SSc
records.text: AFRAM 315 Black Identities and Political Power (5) SSc Relates the deployment of political power within institutions to shifting racial identities. Shows how racial identities both reflect and inflect relations of domination and resistance within and between cultures in the black diaspora. Prerequisite: either AES 150, AFRAM 150, AFRAM 201, or POL S 201. Offered: jointly with POL S 315.
records.prerequisiteText: either AES 150, AFRAM 150, AFRAM 201, or POL S 201.

records.title: Black Literary Genres
records.header: AFRAM 318 Black Literary Genres (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 318 Black Literary Genres (5) A&H, DIV Considers how generic forms and conventions have been discussed and distributed in the larger context of African American, or other African diasporic literary studies. Links the relationship between generic forms to questions of power within social, cultural, and historical contexts. Offered: jointly with ENGL 318; AWSp.

records.title: Black Women in Drama
records.header: AFRAM 320 Black Women in Drama (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 320 Black Women in Drama (5) A&H, DIV Character types of black women as represented in plays by black women. Some black male playwrights are juxtaposed with black female writers for comparative analysis. Playwrights include Georgia Douglas Johnson, Angelina Grimke, Alice Chidress, Lorraine Hansberry, Ira Aldridge, LeRoi Jones.

records.title: History of African American Women and the Feminist Movement
records.header: AFRAM 321 History of African American Women and the Feminist Movement (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 321 History of African American Women and the Feminist Movement (5) SSc, DIV "Feminist Movement" from early nineteenth century to present. Treats relationship between black and white women in their struggle for independence, at times together and at times apart. Discusses the reasons, process, and results of collaboration as well as opposition. Examines recent and contemporary attempts at cooperation. Offered: jointly with GWSS 321.

records.title: Music, Folklore, and Performance in Black Society
records.header: AFRAM 330 Music, Folklore, and Performance in Black Society (5) A&H
records.text: AFRAM 330 Music, Folklore, and Performance in Black Society (5) A&H Focuses on cultural expressions created by people of African descent in the Unites States in the twentieth century, with an emphasis on music, folklore, dance, and humor. Offered: WSp.

records.title: Black Sound Studies and the Archive
records.header: AFRAM 332 Black Sound Studies and the Archive (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 332 Black Sound Studies and the Archive (5) A&H, DIV Explores questions such as: What do official archives remember and forget? How does Black sound create a repository of history and memory where Black people are the makers and shapers of the story? What listening practices does Black sound elicit? Focuses on Black sound studies, including scholarship on race and the voice, music, soundscapes, audio technology, and listening to imagine alternative ways of creating, being, and belonging. Recommended: any AES, AAS, CHSTU, AFRAM, GWSS, or AIS course. Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Civil Rights and Black Power in the United States
records.header: AFRAM 334 Civil Rights and Black Power in the United States (5) A&H/SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 334 Civil Rights and Black Power in the United States (5) A&H/SSc, DIV Examines the politics and culture of the modern African American freedom struggle, which began after WWII and continued into the 1970s. Interrogates political strategies associated with nonviolent direct action, armed self-reliance, and black nationalism, as well as the cultural expression that reflect these political currents. Offered: jointly with HSTAA 334.

records.title: Genre, Gender, and The Black Arts Movement
records.header: AFRAM 335 Genre, Gender, and The Black Arts Movement (5) A&H
records.text: AFRAM 335 Genre, Gender, and The Black Arts Movement (5) A&H Explores the literature, music, visual art, and performing arts of the Black Arts Movement, the sibling of the Black Power Movement. Students engage with in-depth reading assignments and sensory activities. Covers themes such as anti-Black violence, gender roles, self-love, socioeconomic inequity, and Black empowerment. Includes artists such as Larry Neal, Sonia Sanchez, Sun Ra, Katherine Dunham, and Barbara Jones-Hogu. Recommended: AFRAM 101; AFRAM 150/HSTAA 150; and AFRM 334/HSTAA 334.

records.title: Popular Music, Race, Identity, and Social Change
records.header: AFRAM 337 Popular Music, Race, Identity, and Social Change (5) SSc/A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 337 Popular Music, Race, Identity, and Social Change (5) SSc/A&H, DIV Focuses on popular music, shifting formations of race and identity and social change in various cultural, historical, and political contexts. Explores popular music as a tool for social change, a vehicle for community-building and a form of political and aesthetic expression. Course overlaps with: MUSIC 162 and BIS 363.

records.title: The Harlem Renaissance: A Literary Study
records.header: AFRAM 340 The Harlem Renaissance: A Literary Study (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 340 The Harlem Renaissance: A Literary Study (5) A&H, DIV Highlights Harlem Renaissance - 1912 through mid-1930s - as establishing a role for twentieth-century African American writer, encompassing literature, politics, and decolonization of the image of Africa, and solidifying integrationist and nationalist schools of thought. Examines images, themes, and characterizations in creating a literary aesthetic simultaneously American and African American.

records.title: Black Aesthetics
records.header: AFRAM 350 Black Aesthetics (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: AFRAM 350 Black Aesthetics (5) A&H/SSc Draws on both multi-media and print sources, including fiction, poetry, prose, films, polemics, historiography and speeches to explore the idea of a black aesthetic in various cultural, historical, and political contexts within the twentieth century.

records.title: African American Literature
records.header: AFRAM 358 African American Literature (5) A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 358 African American Literature (5) A&H, DIV Selected writings, novels, short stories, plays, and poems by African American and African-descended writers in or from the United States. Study of the historical, cultural, and intellectual context for the development of literary work by such writers, including attention to identity, power, and inequality. Offered: jointly with ENGL 358.

records.title: Black Digital Studies
records.header: AFRAM 360 Black Digital Studies (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 360 Black Digital Studies (5) SSc, DIV Bridges and intersects two interdisciplinary fields - black studies and digital humanities. Attention to knowledge production. Role of archives, collections, research centers, the black press, and digital technology. Ideas related to power, memory, resistance, perspective and respectability politics in storytelling and control of the vehicles used to do so. Recommended: introduction to sociology; and introductory courses in African American studies and communications. Offered: AWSpS.

records.title: African American Political Thought
records.header: AFRAM 370 African American Political Thought (5) SSc
records.text: AFRAM 370 African American Political Thought (5) SSc Political ideologies and philosophies of pivotal African American historical figures and the conditions under which these ideologies are developed, rejected, and transformed. How ideologies relate to solution of African American political problems.

records.title: Health Disparities in Black Women
records.header: AFRAM 380 Health Disparities in Black Women (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 380 Health Disparities in Black Women (5) SSc, DIV Examines how social, economic, environmental, cultural, and lifestyle factors contribute to Black women's persistent and severe health disparities, as well as to disparities in their access to health care, quality of care received, and health insurance coverage. Recommended: any 100-level AFRAM, AES, AAS, or CHSTU course. Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Advanced African American Studies in Humanities
records.header: AFRAM 404 Advanced African American Studies in Humanities (5, max. 15) A&H, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 404 Advanced African American Studies in Humanities (5, max. 15) A&H, DIV Advanced and interdisciplinary engagement with racial formation, Black cultural production, and resistance among people of African descent throughout the Diaspora. Draws upon cultural studies perspectives with an emphasis on literature, film, music, performance, visual and material culture. Topics include art, labor, migration, politics; racial capitalism and political economy; social movements and cultural history; black intellectual traditions. Offered: AWSpS.

records.title: Advanced African American Studies in Social Science
records.header: AFRAM 405 Advanced African American Studies in Social Science (5, max. 15) SSc, DIV
records.text: AFRAM 405 Advanced African American Studies in Social Science (5, max. 15) SSc, DIV Advanced study of racial formation, Black cultural production, and resistance among people of African descent throughout the Diaspora. Social science theories and methods used to examine various topics, including social scientific analysis of political history; social movements; intellectual traditions; theory; and intersections with urban, digital and legal studies; race, science, and biopolitics; public health and environmental studies. Offered: AWSpS.

Statutory and case law which determined role of blacks in American society, and use of law by blacks to gain civil and personal rights.
